The Opportunity

We’re already making this content. We’re just not paying for more of it.

Over the past month, Candace’s social media team has been driving a scrappy, high-energy push to get more of our own people on camera — trend videos, Shay content, behind-the-scenes bits. It’s working. This pilot turns that momentum into a standing incentive, so making DR content becomes something people opt into on purpose, not something we catch on video by accident.

The Proof

The trending, UGC-style videos are the ones actually working

Six consecutive posts on the same account, in order — the pattern shows up immediately.

The two trending videos outperformed everything around them by 10–30x on likes alone — and they’re the only posts in the sequence that generated comments, reposts, and shares. It feels authentic, it feels personal, and it shows the team behind the marketing company Digital Resource is.

We’ll keep a mix of static imagery, but strictly for company updates — we’re hiring, work anniversaries, birthdays, that kind of thing. Those posts still land toward the low end, just not as low as our previous, mostly AI-generated approach.

The Projection

What $800 of trending video could look like

Not every video is solo — some are duo, some are small groups, and each costs different points. Weighting for a realistic mix gets us to a more honest video count than assuming everyone works alone.

Solo videos — 33.33% of mix5 pts each

Small-group videos — 33.33% of mix8 pts each (2 × 4 people, max)

The Mechanics

A simple point system, weighted toward solo effort

Points scale down as group size scales up — solo creators get the full reward, large groups get a team perk instead of diluted points.

SituationPointsNote
Solo video5Full individual reward
Duo video3 eachSlight collaboration bonus over an even split
Small group (3–4)2 eachStill tracked in points
Large group (5+)—Pulled out of points entirely — team perk instead (lunch, shoutout)
Manager-produced video0Counts toward participation, doesn’t earn points
25 pts
Payout threshold — 5 solo videos
$25
Gift card per payout
No cap
Points never expire
The Budget

Funded from budget we already have

No new line item. Roughly $100 is allocated per participating team, pulled from the marketing budget they already have. Payouts only fire when someone actually produces qualifying content, so cost scales with output, not headcount. The exchange rate is simple: 1 point = $1.

Show your work

Payout threshold (25 pts)$25 gift card
Marketing budget per team$100
Payouts that covers4 × $25
8 service teams × $100$800 total

Payout method: Visa gift card, or Tremendous for remote team members.

If a team blows through its $100, that’s not a budget problem — it means dramatically more video got made than we planned for, which is exactly the kind of top-of-funnel activity that turns into pipeline. Overspend here is a leading indicator of success, not a risk.
Quality Control

Every video clears one approval gate before it counts

Four steps, three sets of eyes — creative fit, then social fit — before anything gets published or earns points.

DR team member · creates → Creative · initial review → Candace · final review → Social media team · publishes → ✓Live
Operations

Tracked automatically, not by hand

We’re building an internal platform to log submissions, tally points, and track payout status — not a spreadsheet someone has to babysit. For a small, curated Phase 1 roster, that build stays deliberately simple; it can grow more sophisticated once this scales past the pilot.

Phase 1 Roster

Invite-only, on purpose

This isn’t open enrollment. Richard, Candace, and other team managers hand-pick who’s invited, prioritizing people they believe will actually deliver consistent content. We’re deliberately not opening this company-wide yet — the roster should feel a little exclusive, a signal that this isn’t just handed out. We’re not looking to put out slop.

Phase 1 · Now

Invite-only

Richard, Candace, and managers select the roster directly, based on who they believe will actually deliver.

Someday · Later

Earned access

Once the pilot proves out, anyone can apply: submit social videos you’ve already made, and if the quality holds up, you’re in. Same bar, different door.

The Ask

Approve the Phase 1 pilot

A hand-picked roster, funded at $800 total across our 8 service teams (~$100 each) from budget we already have, tracked on our own platform, and gated by one clear approval step before any point is earned.

Approve Phase 1 Pilot
  • Curated roster — Richard, Candace, and managers choose who’s invited, not open enrollment
  • $800 total, 8 service teams × $100 each, existing marketing budget, no new spend
  • Tracked automatically on our internal platform, no manual spreadsheets
  • One approval gate: creator → Creative review → Candace’s final review → social media team publishes
  • 1 point = $1, 25 points = $25, points never expire
  • Projected upside if fully used: ~126 videos (weighted for a realistic solo/duo/group mix), ~250,000 views
